title: Noob here; recommended plan for creating mods for games or creating games?
author: ChubbyNunu
selftext:
My partner plays some of those “Supermarket simulator” and “library cleanup” genre of games, but wishes they had certain features or items in the game. 

I know next to nothing about coding, so im hoping that Ai would be able to help me with this. 

Do you have any recommendations for what models or plans to purchase for creating mods/games? 

As for a side question; when you buy a monthly subscription, do you have unlimited tokens? I’ve seen on this sub someone made a minecraft mod which cost 2000$ worth of tokens, did they have to buy 2000 work of tokens?

Thank you for any advice

comments.author: LucidFir
comments.body:
the posts titled "tHiS gAmE cOsT $2k" seem to always be referring to token cost if you were going through the API pay as you go. whilst I guess that maybe that's a more consistent measure, they're likely not paying that much as they're certainly using the bulk discount of a monthly sub.

no you don't get unlimited tokens. I've built https://urchinskipper.itch.io/ in 3 weeks now maxing out an astra 5x sub. I'll take a break for the next 2 months due to work and see what the best model is in December. hopefully one that understands UX, UI, and HUD design

comments.author: HaMMeReD
comments.body:
Get a Claude or Codex subscription whatever you can afford.

No, there is no unlimited plan, not unless you have some kind of privilege or self-host LLMs.

I have the $200 codex plan. In the last 7 days I used $750 in api equivalent spend. So I get about $3000 worth of token a month if you use api equivalent as your measuring stick. I use pretty much 100% of the plan 100% of the time now. 

That said, the values of these plans is constantly changing, and I'd recommend starting with a $20 claude plan and seeing how far it gets you. API Equivalent value is pretty meaningless indicator unless you are watching your usage/budget. Even if you use Codex/Claude the cost of models directly affect you.
